A.W. Bhuiyan, Additional Attorney General instructed by B. Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the respondent

Golam Sarwar Kamal
Vs.
The State
full_judgment:
Fazle Monim, C.J: This appeal arises from a judgment of a Bench of the High Court Division, Barisal, passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1984 rejecting the prayer for anticipatory bail of the appellant under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 2. The appellant is a candidate for chairmanship of No. 4 Dautala Union Parishad. P.S. Bamna. District Patuakhali. On 29 December 1983 the Union Parishad election for the chairman and members of the Union started but the election of Word No. 1 was stopped as a result of illegal activities or the contesting candidates. The election of this Ward was to be held at some future date. In Ward Nos. 2 and 3 election had been completed. Appellant got 1549 votes and his nearest rival got 683 votes only. A day before the election one of his supporters, Nur Islam, was killed on the spot by gun shot, but the attempt to kill the appellant failed. Bamna P.S. Case No. 1(12)83 under section 302 of the Penal Code was started by Abdus Sattar, the brother of the victim. Though in the First Information Report no allegation has been made against the appellant, his enemies were trying to implicate him in the case. The appellant apprehended that the police being influenced by his enemies may arrest him so that he may no longer participate in the election to be held in respect of Ward No. 1. Further, he will be humiliated in the estimation of the voters. His enemies had also successfully induced the complainant of the aforesaid case to swear an affidavit implicating the appellant for the murder of his brother. The police had already come to his house several times, the last being on January 13, 1984 and also arrested one of his servants in order to know the appellants whereabouts. 

 3. Appellant moved the High Court Division for granting anticipatory bail which was refused by the learned Judges holding that the appellant's apprehension that his opponents in the ensuing election were conspiring to implicate him in a false case to prevent him from doing his election-campaign is rather farfetched. Being aggrieved the appellant moved this Court and obtained leave to appeal on the ground that although there was no allegation against him in the F.I.R., there were sufficient circumstances on the basis of which the appellant apprehended that at the instance of his election rivals the police may impress him so that he might not actively work for his election campaign. 

 4. Khondker Mahbub Hossain, Advocate For the appellant submitted that the appellant's apprehensions were not without any foundation since the appellant was leading in the election of Wards No. 2 and 3 over his rivals by a comfortable majority and expected to lead also in the election of Word No. 1 which stands postponed. If he could now be humiliated in the eyes of the voters by getting him arrested by the police, his rivals could defeat him quite easily. Secondly, there had been a murder and the aforesaid police case was started. Every effort was now being made by his rivals to implicate him in it and the police had already raided his house and arrested one of his servants. Khondker Mahbub Hossain submitted that in veto of these circumstances it could not be said that the appellant's apprehensions of arrest in order to debar his further participation in the election of Ward No. 1 were baseless. 

 5. From the fails stated in the petition and the circumstances mentioned therein, it appears that the appellant may reasonably apprehend that the police might arrest him to prevent his participation in the election. Resort to ingenious devices to thwart the possibility of winning the election is not unknown. Whether his implication in the murder case, even if made. would lead to his arrest and end in his ultimate conviction may or may not the true. Fact is that, if in the circumstances mentioned above when it appears that the election of one of the Wards stands postponed for a while, his arrest would dim or even destroy the chances of his winning the election. We are told that the postponed election of Ward No. 1 would be held soon. Criminal Prosecution, even if it has just started cannot be stifled. Nor should the political activities during such very brief interval as in the instant case be restrained even by the possibility of resorting to process of criminal prosecution. Such process may have free play and go on as usual as soon as the postponed election would be held.
